messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: mean variance relationship in stan
parts:
Hi,

Does anybody have experience of using mean-variance relationship in stan?  In the frequentist domain I found an article on this: http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378375810002764.  Is there some analog procedure in the Bayesian domain?  The problem I have in mind is related to counts and neither Poisson or negative binomial distribution provides satisfactory results.  For example, what to do if the Var[Y]=phi*E[Y]^lambda.  It would be great to estimate phi and lambda from the data.

Thank you,
Linas

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] mean variance relationship in stan
parts:
You can just use

increment_log_prob(log_lik)

it's vectorized.

To make the model hierarchical, you replace your fixed priors on
A and B_raw with models for which you estimate the hierarchical
variance.

If at all possible, never apply exp() directly. I see there's
an exp() on phi. You could just use a lognormal, since you're
coding up a log normal indirectly, but that's probably not going
to help since there's an implicit exp() transform anyway.

- Bob

With lognormal you need to constrain the parameter to be positive.
And if you're initializing by hand, you need positive initial
values.

> On Apr 4, 2015, at 7:55 AM, Linas Mockus <linasm...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Bob,
>
> Thanks a lot. Sorry for my writing style with too many spaces - it was burned into my bones 30 years ago.

>
> My questions are:
> - Did I make model hierarchical enough to handle very significant heteroscedasticity?

That's a different issue. You need either a time series or
predictors of the variation.
> - How to compare poisson pseudo likelihood results with the ones from this model? I want to prove to my frequuentist colleagues that Bayes is the way to go

I don't know what pseudolikelihood is.

We like to compare models using predictions, such as cross-validation.
But if they're frequentist they're probably not doing predictions
with their model estimates.

One of the main advantages of Bayesian inference is how simple it
is to do inference incorporating information about the data generating
process (scientific/domain-specific and measurement related).
> - How to check if heteroscedasticity is handled better than poisson pseudo likelihood
This would be rolled into any predictive evaluation.
> - Does it make sense to leave miu_phi parameter since it looks insignificant

It shouldn't hurt if you do full Bayesian inference and may
help with uncertainty.
> - Any other comments how to improve the code

Looks like it's mixing well as is. I don't think those are the
traces that go with the model you sent, though, because there's no
little "a" in the model. Also, you might want a fatter prior on
mu_A given that it's estimated value is around 10, though that's
still consistent with a normal(0,5) prior.

- Bob
